title: Country Code vs Area Code: The Difference
h1: Country code vs area code: what's the difference?
description: Country code vs area code: a country code picks the country, an area code picks the region within it. Learn how to tell them apart and look up either.
faq: Is 212 a country code or an area code?

Both, depending on context. As a US area code, 212 covers New York City. As an international calling code, +212 is Morocco. The + sign is the giveaway: +212 dialed with a plus reaches Morocco, while 212 inside a +1 number is New York.
How do I know if a number uses a country code?

Look at the start. A number beginning with + or 00 opens with a country calling code, such as +44 or +212. If there is no plus sign and the number has the local length (ten digits in the US and Canada), it has no country code — the first three digits are the area code instead.
Where can I look up a country code or area code?

Use Insight Dial's free directories. The country calling code directory has a page for every country and code, and the area code directory (or the area code lookup tool) covers every US and Canadian area code with its location and current local time.
body:
If you have ever stared at a phone number and wondered whether 212 means New York or Morocco, you are not alone. Country codes and area codes are both number prefixes, they can even share the same digits, and mixing them up is one of the most common dialing mistakes. Here is the difference in plain terms.

What a country code is

A country calling code tells the phone network which country you want to reach. You dial it after the + sign (or your exit code, often 00), before the local number. Examples are +1 for the United States and Canada, +44 for the United Kingdom, +91 for India and +212 for Morocco. Every country has one, and you can look any of them up in the free country calling code directory.

What an area code is

An area code sits inside a country and points to a region, city or number type. In the United States and Canada it is the three digits that come right after +1 — for example 415 for San Francisco or 212 for New York City. Browse them all in the US and Canada area code directory, or type one into the area code lookup tool to see its state, time zone and current local time.

Why the same digits can mean both

This is where people get caught out. The digits 212 are a well-known example: as a US area code, 212 covers New York City, while as an international calling code +212 belongs to Morocco. Same three digits, completely different meaning. The + sign is what separates them — a leading + (or 00) marks a country code, while an area code appears later inside the number.

How to tell them apart quickly

  • A number that starts with + or 00 begins with a country code.
  • Once you reach +1, the next three digits are a US or Canadian area code.
  • No plus sign and ten digits? In North America that is usually area code plus local number, with no country code at all.
  • Still unsure? Look the prefix up: the calling code directory covers countries and the area code directory covers US and Canadian regions.

Why it matters if you run on phone calls

For a business that buys or routes calls, telling a country code from an area code is not trivia — it decides where a caller goes. Insight Dial reads each caller's country and region automatically, routes them to a buyer licensed for that area, and records every call as searchable data. Explore the free tools or the full area code and calling code directories to see the data behind it.
